name: Insulin aspart
mechanism: Rapid-onset insulin for prandial glucose control
dosing: Doses individualized; given at mealtimes or by pump
contraindications: Hypoglycaemia or hypersensitivity to insulin or excipients
interactions: Many drugs affect glucose control — e.g., corticosteroids may increase glucose, beta-blockers may blunt hypoglycaemia symptoms; adjust insulin dose accordingly
monitoring: Frequent blood glucose monitoring during initiation and titration, and when other interacting drugs or acute illness occur; monitor for hypoglycaemia
pregnancy: Insulin is the preferred agent for glycaemic control in pregnancy when needed; follow obstetric guidance
sideEffects: Hypoglycaemia, injection-site reactions, weight gain; rare allergic reactions
clinicalPearls: Rapid-acting analogue given at mealtimes to control post-prandial glucose; dosing should be individualized with education on carbohydrate counting and hypoglycaemia management
indication: Prandial insulin therapy for glycaemic control in type 1 diabetes and as required in type 2 diabetes
